source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
NTT VA7 publishes 36 MW of IT capacity across 125,000 square feet of technical space in Ashburn, Virginia. That works out to roughly 288 watts per square foot of technical space, a density consistent with a mix of enterprise and high-performance workloads rather than a purpose-built hyperscale shell. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 36 MW of IT load is roughly 900 racks; at a more conservative 10 kW per rack, typical of legacy enterprise deployments, the same power supports around 3,600 racks. The operator has not published a rack count, a cooling architecture, or a power usage effectiveness figure, so which end of that range the campus actually operates toward is not determinable from the published data.

No certifications appear in the published specifications for this facility, so no certification-based qualification can be read from the data.

Among the 326 data center facilities mapped in Virginia, only 19 have published a megawatt figure on their operator spec pages. VA7's 36 MW places it twelfth among those 19 by published IT capacity, in a state whose 19 publishing facilities together declare 1,326 MW, meaning VA7 accounts for roughly 2.7 percent of that published total. Ashburn is the densest data center market in Virginia and among the densest in the world, so a twelfth-place rank within the publishing subset still locates this campus in highly contested, infrastructure-rich territory. Whether the remaining 307 mapped Virginia facilities carry more or less capacity than VA7 is unknown, because they have not published figures this site has read.
